card.title: Clauses and modals — complex sentences, shaded meaning

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Class 12 grammar compounds Class 11: clauses (main + subordinate: noun/adjective/adverbial) build simple/compound/complex/compound-complex sentences; modals shade meaning (can/could/may/might/must/should/would — ability, permission, obligation, probability); conditionals grade reality; punctuation (comma splices, apostrophes, reported-speech marks) and capitalisation carry meaning-level marks.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: sentence ladder: simple (1 clause) · compound (FANBOYS join) · complex (subordinator: because/although/which/who) · compound-complex (both)  ·  modals: can (ability) · may (permission/possibility) · must (obligation/deduction) · should (advice) · would (habit/request)  ·  punctuation: , ; : ' " " . ? ! — each with one job

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Subordinators create dependence (remove the main clause and fragments result). Modal choice follows function, not tense (past modals = could/would/might have + V3 for counterfactuals). Comma splices need conjunctions, semicolons or full stops — never bare commas between independent clauses.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Restrictive vs non-restrictive relatives (that vs which with commas) change meaning: 'students who cheat fail' vs 'students, who cheat, fail'. Dangling modifiers ('Walking home, the rain soaked me') attach to the wrong subject — NEB's favourite correction. Apostrophes mark possession/contraction, never plurals.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Combine with a clause: 'He is rich. He is unhappy.' → concessive complex: 'Although he is rich, he is unhappy.' Modal shade: 'You must submit' (obligation) vs 'You should submit' (advice) vs 'You may submit' (permission) — same verb, three forces, chosen by intent.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Sentence-type labels describe structure, not quality (a perfect simple sentence beats a tangled complex one). Modal 'rules' bend in politeness ('Might I suggest…') and dialects. Punctuation guides prosody but cannot rescue incoherent thought.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From kernel sentences outward: deploy coordination (equal ideas, FANBOYS) vs subordination (unequal ideas, subordinators) by INFORMATION hierarchy — main clause carries the news, subordinate clauses carry background. Modals derive from speaker stance toward reality (possible/necessary/advisable), mapped onto the standard nine.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Joining two sentences? Equal weight → FANBOYS; unequal → subordinator. Modal blanks: obligation→must, advice→should, possibility→may/might, past counterfactual→would/could have V3. Punctuation: splice→semicolon, possession→apostrophe, direct speech→quotes+comma+capital.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: sentence combining with clause types; modal gap-fills by function; error correction (dangling modifiers, splices, apostrophes); reported-speech + conditional revision pairs.
